blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
A surface photographed under even light presents nearly the same appearance from every angle; the same surface under uneven light does not. Exposure changes between views, illumination varies within a single image, and locally strong light sources leave one region bright and its neighbor in shadow. Multi-view reconstruction methods such as 3D Gaussian Splatting treat these lighting artifacts as if they were properties of the scene, entangling capture-specific illumination with the geometry and color they recover. We present EvenSplat, a framework that separates the two. EvenSplat couples an image-space illumination decomposition with an illumination field carried by the Gaussians, so that the same explanation of the lighting is shared between the two-dimensional and three-dimensional views of the scene; a camera-response network and a local exposure-compensation module absorb the global and residual differences that remain across training images. Through extensive experiments across multiple datasets and diverse forms of uneven illumination (cross-view exposure, spatial illumination variation, and high-contrast lighting) on both real-world captured and simulated benchmarks,
EvenSplat generally outperforms state-of-the-art methods, particularly under high-contrast illumination.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Photographs of the same scene are rarely taken under the same light. A camera’s exposure adapts from shot to shot ( Shim et al., 2014 ) , a flash or a window lights one side of an object more than the other ( Debevec and Malik, 1997 ) , and a bright sky or lamp splits a single frame into washed-out and shadowed regions ( Petschnigg et al., 2004 ) . For a human these differences are unremarkable; for a system that reconstructs a scene from many such photographs, they are a problem. Each image reports a different brightness and color for the same physical surface, and the reconstruction is left to reconcile observations that no longer agree.
blocks.zh: 同一场景的照片很少在同一光下拍摄. 摄像头的曝光从镜头到镜头(Shim等人,2014年),闪光灯或窗光灯的一面比另一面要多(Debevec和Malik,1997年),亮的天空或灯光将单个帧分割成被冲走和被阴影的区域(Petschnigg等人,2004年). 对于一个人类来说,这些差异是无足轻重的;对于一个从许多这样的照片中重建一个场景的系统来说,这是一个问题。 每张图像都报告同一物理表面有不同的亮度和颜色,重建则留待调和不再同意的观测结果.

blocks.en:
Novel View Synthesis (NVS) methods such as Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) ( Mildenhall et al., 2020 ) and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) ( Kerbl et al., 2023 ) reconstruct such scenes with high fidelity, but they assume photometric consistency across views. When the inputs disagree, fitting them faithfully entangles the lighting of each capture with the geometry and color of the scene, so the recovered model carries the artifacts of how it was photographed rather than what was photographed.
These inconsistencies take three characteristic forms: Cross-View Exposure Variation (CEV) , as when a camera re-meters between shots; Spatial Illumination Variation
(SIV) within a single view, as under a flash or a side window; and High-Contrast
Illumination (HCI) with strong bright–dark imbalance, as under a harsh local light source. The first is a property of the camera, the latter two of the scene, but all three break the photometric agreement that reconstruction relies on (Fig. 1 ).

To evaluate these conditions beyond digital image perturbations, we assembled
a nine-scene real-world dataset with exposure-bracketed and flash-illuminated
captures. It covers the three settings with three CEV, four SIV, and two HCI
scenes, together with evenly illuminated reference captures for appearance evaluation. This dataset
forms a central part of our evaluation, complemented by controlled simulated
benchmarks and a directional-lighting robustness experiment.

blocks.en:
We introduce EvenSplat , a coupled 2D–3D appearance decomposition
framework inspired by the reflect- ance–illumination factorization of Retinex
theory ( Land, 1977 ) . Its central design is to use an image-space decomposition optimized together with the Gaussian
representation. A multi-scale network
predicts per-image illumination and derives a base-appearance estimate, while
a Gaussian-level illumination field predicts illumination coefficients
conditioned on position, surface normal, and viewing direction. Aligning the
image-space and rendered illumination maps connects the two branches.
Our contributions are:
(1) A coupled 2D–3D decomposition framework that transfers online
image-space illumination guidance to a Gaussian-level illumination field
for reconstruction from exposure- and illumination-inconsistent inputs.
(2) An image-specific correction combining global camera response and illumination-guided local exposure compensation for residual variation in training views.
(3) A nine-scene real-world captured dataset spanning cross-view exposure
variation, spatial illumination variation, and high-contrast illumination,
with reference captures for evaluating appearance reconstruction.

blocks.en: 2.1 NVS in Challenging Lighting Conditions

blocks.en:

that violate the photometric consistency assumed by standard NeRF and 3DGS.
NeRF-W ( Martin-Brualla et al., 2021 ) introduced per-image appearance
embeddings for unconstrained photo collections. GS-W, SWAG, and WildGaussians ( Zhang et al., 2024a ; Dahmani et al., 2024 ; Kulhánek et al., 2024 ) transfer this
idea to Gaussian scenes, while WildSplat and WilLaGS ( Zhang et al., 2026 ; Bai et al., 2026 ) address unposed or strongly
appearance-varying inputs.

blocks.en:
Even these advances remain brittle in extreme spatially uneven lighting, for instance, scenes with severe cross-view exposure discontinuities, mixed HDR regions, and strong, locally varying light sources across large indoor spaces. In such cases, appearance changes overwhelm per-image embeddings or local feature transfers and drive spurious densification or residual tone inconsistency.
EvenSplat considers CEV, SIV, and HCI in one
formulation without requiring calibrated light geometry. Instead of aiming to recover a full BRDF or a physically calibrated light, EvenSplat learns an illumination-consistent base appearance for novel-view synthesis by coupling image-space decomposition with
a shared Gaussian illumination field while retaining the efficient, explicit
rendering structure of 3DGS.

blocks.en: 2.2 Image-Space Illumination Decomposition
blocks.zh: 2.2 图像空间照明分解

blocks.en:
Retinex theory ( Land and McCann, 1971 ) separates observed appearance into reflectance and illumination. RetinexNet, KinD, and
URetinex-Net ( Wei et al., 2018 ; Zhang et al., 2019 ; Wu et al., 2022 ) replace
handcrafted decomposition priors with learned illumination estimation for
low-light enhancement. Later work broadens the restoration model:
Retinexformer ( Cai et al., 2023 ) uses illumination-guided attention;
RetinexMamba and ECMamba ( Bai et al., 2024 ; Dong et al., 2024 ) employ
state-space architectures; and Fourier, video, and diffusion formulations
address mixed exposure and general illumination degradation ( Huang et al., 2022a ; Liu et al., 2024 ; He et al., 2025 ) .

处理混合接触和一般照明降解问题(Huang等人,2022a); 刘等人,2024年;He等人,2025年).

blocks.en:
Beyond Retinex, intrinsic image decomposition methods separate surface appearance from shading rather than
directly producing an enhanced photograph. Recent work
extends the classical albedo–shading formulation toward more complex
illumination and richer intrinsic properties ( Careaga and Aksoy, 2024 ; Dirik et al., 2026 ) .
Related multi-view inverse-rendering work further models material, spatial illumination, and camera response from captured images ( Lin et al., 2025 ) .
These decomposition-based formulations motivate our image-space branch, which
separates illumination from base appearance and uses the resulting
decomposition to guide the learning of a shared 3D Gaussian illumination
representation.

在Retinex之外,内在的图像分解方法将表面外观与阴影区分开来而不是
直接制作增强照片。 最近的工作

blocks.en: 4 Experiments
blocks.zh: 4 实验

blocks.en:
We test the central claim behind EvenSplat: coupling image-space priors with a
shared 3D illumination model is most useful when photometric variation cannot
be explained by a global per-view correction. We evaluate physically captured
CEV, SIV, and HCI scenes, repeat the comparison under controlled perturbations,
and use cross-lighting and component ablations to probe what is learned.
blocks.zh:
我们测试EvenSplate背后的中心主张:将图像空间前身与一个
共享的 3D 照明模型在光度变化不能时最有用
以全局逐景校正来解释。 我们评估一下实际捕获的
CEV,SIV,和HCI的场景,重复在控制扰动下进行比较,
并使用交叉光线和元件喷发来探测学到的知识。

Our nine-scene benchmark contains three Cross-View Exposure Variation (CEV),
four Spatial Illumination Variation (SIV), and two High-Contrast Illumination
(HCI) scenes spanning indoor and outdoor subjects. Unlike a purely synthetic
benchmark, these captures retain camera response, highlight saturation, flash
falloff, and cast shadows. A second collection under more uniform illumination
provides an appearance reference for each scene.

blocks.en:
EvenSplat couples image-space decomposition with shared Gaussian
illumination and global–local view-specific correction. Across physical and
simulated benchmarks, its largest gains occur under spatially uneven and
high-contrast illumination, where global appearance models are insufficient;
ablations confirm that the 2D and 3D branches are
complementary. The result is a practical route to more
illumination-consistent Gaussian scene representations from ordinary sRGB
captures. Limitations include sRGB-domain ambiguity and saturation, the
training-image-specific ILEC parameters, and unmodeled specularities, motion
blur, and sensor noise.

Training-image embeddings and ILEC maps are image specific and are not assigned
to held-out views. At inference, the CRN is replaced by the identity response
and the ILEC gain is fixed to one; novel-view rendering therefore relies only
on the shared Gaussian representation and the learned 3D illumination field.
All methods are trained and evaluated on the same input data and paired
held-out views. PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS are computed directly between rendered
images and their corresponding references. Unless otherwise stated, no
test-time pose refinement, exposure fitting, affine RGB correction, or color
matching is applied; corrected metrics are retained only as diagnostics and
are excluded from the primary comparisons.

blocks.en:
We follow the publicly released implementations and their native inference
protocols. For 3DGS, we use the default gsplat configuration. For 3DGS+CHROMA, we use the official CHROMA implementation to harmonize the training images in batches of up to 500 images, and then train 3DGS on the corrected images using the same default gsplat configuration. For GS-W, we enable its per-image appearance optimization during training and render
held-out views from the learned intrinsic/base appearance representation,
without optimizing an additional appearance code for the test image. For
Bilateral Grid, per-image bilateral grids are used only during training to
absorb view-specific photometric discrepancies; the correction branch is
bypassed for held-out views, which are rendered directly from the learned 3D
representation. Luminance-GS is evaluated with its released view-adaptive
configuration, while PPISP uses its released post-processing pipeline together
with the MCMC Gaussian strategy. We do not introduce zero, mean, nearest-view,
or other appearance-code heuristics beyond those defined by the corresponding
released methods.

ILEC models image-specific spatial exposure residuals that remain after
Gaussian-level illumination modeling. The module-level ablation in

local model rather than an unconstrained per-image correction map.

blocks.en:
EvenSplat maintains high-quality full-scene observation rendering, achieving 37.6-dB PSNR on average and remaining visually comparable to methods dedicated
to fitting the illuminated observations. As shown in Table 12 , its additional decomposition output
has the highest base-appearance PSNR on all four scenes, improving mean PSNR
from 13.23 dB for the strongest baseline to 17.91 dB. SSIM and LPIPS remain
mixed, particularly on CatRoom , so the improvement should be read as
better recovery of the uniform-light target rather than a universal perceptual
advantage. This is because in regions saturated by the same strong global light in every view,
clamping removes the original color information from the entire observation
set. No reconstruction method can identify those colors without additional
measurements or priors; this limitation comes from the dataset observations,
